characters.summary: Cóemgen an t-Éigse Measceal (COE-muh-gen), newly gauntleted, looking his age: a manaim, who keeps the hours but has not taken a monk's full vows and may marry. He longs to marry and raise a family on Great Saltee, crossing to the covenant each day, but there is no unwed woman on the island, and his Gift and crippling shyness spoil his hopes. Gentle and likeable, he may one day row to Wexford to carry off a bride, or court a woman he meets, earnestly and clumsily.

characters.name: Dáire Cú Ua Dáire Ua Mearcaire

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: The unGifted leader of Leth Cuinn, who looks sixty-three; he took the house from his father, Dáire Direach, and is shaping his eldest son, Dáire an Chogaidh, to follow him. He is ritually wed to Úathach, and since his mortal wife died the marriage has been more than a form. He has nothing but scorn for the Redcaps of Leth Moga, and thinks their leader too doddering and bookish to lead the Tribunal's Redcaps.

characters.name: Dáire an Chogaidh Mac Dáire Cú

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Dáire Cú's eldest son, an unGifted Redcap who looks forty-eight. In his macgnímartha he fought de Courcy's English with the army of Ulster, which is how he got his name, 'of the wars'. He is against everything English and has even voted at Tribunal, for all his House's custom of neutrality; it has made him something of a celebrity, and the primus of House Mercere is rumoured to be readying an answer.

He is more often on the drill ground with warriors than out on Ireland's roads, which is just where his father, well aware of his temper, wants him: a superb, frightening drill-master.

characters.name: Elen Bhodhar inghean Dáire Cú Ua Mearcaire

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Elen the Deaf, youngest of Dáire Cú's five children, an unGifted Redcap of nineteen. Her mother died bearing her, and she was born without hearing; she reads lips perfectly and speaks through mime and a rough sign language. She has just finished her Redcap training and begun to ride Ireland's roads.

characters.name: Cantarus an t-Iarbiteon

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Master of the Songs, the head of Qui Sonant, for fifty years without a challenger; a magus of Jerbiton who looks eighty-five, born in the covenant and seldom outside it since. He knows death or Twilight is not far off, but has found no heir to trust with the covenant: most of the apprentices he has trained have walked away from Qui Sonant's burden, and only Finn remains, who has the wish to lead but not the gift.

characters.name: Finn Mac Cantarus an t-Iarbiteon

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Cantarus's filius, of Jerbiton, who looks thirty-five. He has a gift for Vitae Magorum in Irish, and his histories of the Order are read all over Hibernia; he cares deeply for his covenant and the peace and fellowship it stands for.

He takes it for granted that, as Cantarus's only filius at the covenant, he will be the next Master of the Songs, and has no idea of his pater's doubts. So he learns nothing from his mistakes as a leader, talks freely of his coming rank, and buys friends with long-term promises on the strength of it. He took Lewis's side when the two Verditius quarrelled.

characters.name: Lewis Cultas Bhéardaoiteas

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Master Stonemason of Qui Sonant, of Verditius, who looks fifty. There were two Verditius stonemasons here until they fell out over whether Ingasia may call itself Verditius's domus magna; to cool the quarrel Finn sided with Lewis, and Peter chose to leave. Lewis offers younger Verditius Initiation into the House Mysteries, but only if they declare for Verdi, and such Initiates may find themselves caught in the vendetta his exiled rival is about to widen.

He would pay well for an apprentice with a talent for craft magic, and within a few years will probably go to the Coill Trí seeking one of the seven Gifted children they owe each Tribunal; he will even warn rivals off the child, which Peter, now wandering, may turn against him.

characters.name: Turlough Cultas Críothamon

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Turlough of Criamon, who looks fifty-five, governs the cemetery, the funeral rites and the protection of the spirits in the covenant's keeping, and is well thought of inside the covenant and out. His own magic is the summoning of spirits. He has trained one apprentice and won another at the last Tribunal through his warm relations with the Coill Trí.
characters.secrets: He feels there is more to gain from the spirits than summoning them, and fears his sodales will learn of this growing interest, so any help must come from outside; he would gladly bargain his influence with the Coill Trí for it.

characters.name: Éinri mac Cillíni mich Dáire Boircech

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Vigil's leader, though not its eldest, a magus of Merinita who looks sixty: he keeps the bees, rules the herds and holds the black pig's tusks. Big and bearded, he goes in velvet hung with gold and silver chains, and eats and drinks more than his humours can bear and suffers gout; the spell he invented for it dulls the pain but sours his temper, which he blames on his wife's nagging. His huge court is the centre of the covenant, its kitchens full of cooks thanks to endless silver and its halls full of guests, Hermetic, faerie, magical and mundane. He loves stories, above all tales from beyond Ireland, and gives away his bees' honey, among the best in Hibernia, to friends and allies.

His wife Aoife, kept young by strong longevity rituals, looks far younger than he. They have lately adopted a small boy into Vigil's court, whom Éinri means for House Mercere, so he may need a sponsor at one of the Mercer Houses. His talisman is a coat of bronze mail enchanted to grow with his girth; his familiar a big, lazy wolfhound. His parens Cillíni once taught a Scottish magus, Bróccín, the courtesy owed to Ireland's otherworld, a tale Éinri likes to tell.

He has a long feud with Dalton Ballaugh of Lámbaird: many certamen and clashes of their grogs, not yet Wizard War, but real loathing, odd to onlookers given how alike the two men and their covenants are, and perhaps that is the trouble.

characters.name: Gráinne inghean Uaitéar

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A maga of Merinita, as boisterous as anyone at Vigil, who looks thirty-eight. She married the handsome Pádraig when both were young. Her familiar is a red kite named Úna, whose senses she shares, and her talisman a bow of many materials attuned to several effects, her second: tired of her first, a sword, she broke it in a rite and threw the pieces off the cliffs of Cionn Mhálanna. The same excess runs through her magic, for she is a Waster of Vis without much knowing it.

As quartermaster, a mostly ceremonial post, she must approve any large spending of vis, and she has charge of the vaults and their uncatalogued treasures, though like those before her she has never grown into it and has little notion what they are worth. She knows of the Verditius right to work at Vigil, which may give her the leverage to win one of the Gifted children from Connacht when the Tribunal next meets. The Two Dozen Men of Mhálanna are devoted to her. Guillaume of Praesis, whom she has slighted many times, longs to see her humbled.

characters.name: Máel-ruanaid an Doire

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Vigil's loremaster, of Merinita, who looks fifty: keeper of the covenant's magical traditions, a trust he takes more seriously than those before him, who let many books rot in the vaults, and the mystagogue of Merinita's Folk Mysteries for his sodales. His master taught him divination, the secret of Banbha's Crown, and spells to command the covenant's bees, guide their flight and use their senses; when he seems to know the unknowable, that is likely how.

A master of Merinita Story Magic, he understands the power of symbols and believes Qui Sonant's magic rests not on the songs but on the symbolic act of singing; if he could learn it, the symbols of the Folk Mysteries might be freed from needing a physical form. His fellows find him a little dull, without their sense of fun. His familiar is an owl of like temper; his talisman a skull he found in the vaults and plated in silver.

characters.name: Maoilfhinnéin mac Lir

params.group: the faerie and magical courts of the sea

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: The Ambassador to the Sea, a magus of Merinita who looks fifty and spends much of his time at faerie and magical courts. His talisman is a staff of sea-unicorn horn, his familiar a porpoise, and his wife a faerie princess of Inishtrahull. With his long white hair and beard and his sturdy frame he looks like some old sea god, a likeness he plays up to keep eyes off what he is really doing.
characters.secrets: He believes the old stories must repeat, that the Ordo Hiberniae will be driven back as the native wizards were, and sees the first signs already. Should Vigil come under threat, all is ready for the cathach to go to Inishtrahull and the covenant to be rebuilt on the island. Meanwhile he backs Lámbaird's views at Tribunal to mend the harm Éinri has done; he feeds Gráinne's overconfidence, knowing a sacrifice may soon be needed; and his allies in the sea have brought him the shards of her first talisman, which he has fixed as an Arcane Connection and is steering into the hands of Guillaume of Praesis.

characters.name: Ballack

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Lord of Praesis, a Tytalus from the Rhine who looks sixty-five; Holzner was his filius. He delighted in turning Hibernia's own customs on the Irish and taking his revenge on Meadhbh, yet it says something of him that Holzner's head still hangs from the palisade exactly where she hung it. He despises the Irish magi and their old ways, and is courting the established English covenants and the newcomers alike.

He has spent the past year tightening his grip on the ruins, but the war cost him dearly. His own resources are gone, he owes vis and favours to a number of magi, and he has had to borrow more vis and casting tablets from far-off backers. For all his swagger he knows his prize is only on loan until he pays, so he is hunting for a way to make the covenant pay its way; he cannot be seen to give it up.

characters.name: Báetáin Ua Traimair

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
The traitor of Praesis, who looks forty-seven: one of the besieged, he lost faith in Meadhbh as the siege grew hopeless and, choosing a Praesis that survived over one destroyed, handed the Gáe Bulg to Ballack. When the others found out, they knew the fight was lost and fled.

One of the few Irish-born magi of House Tremere, he has spent his whole life at Praesis; years ago his parens went into retirement at Coeris and took Báetáin's sigil with him. He seldom leaves the old tower now, for every walk takes him past the burnt homes of people he knew, and he still hears their screams as fire fell from the sky; he lives under one roof with Guillaume, who killed them. Still, Praesis stands, and can be rebuilt.

characters.name: Guillaume of Normandy

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Guillaume Flambeau of Normandy, who looks fifty-two. He could never get out from under the shadow of Montverte, where he was apprenticed, and came to Hibernia ten years ago to make his name, drawn by stories heard as an apprentice. He is frighteningly good with Ignem. He has already taken the cathach of an independent magus, and with it that magus's resources and his apprentice, whom he is shaping in his own image.

He is striking at places in Connacht through the Bréifne mercenaries he pays, who find vis sources and raid them; he has not crossed the border himself yet. Gráinne inghean Uaitéar of Vigil has long been his rival, and he would love to see the witch brought low before him.

characters.name: Cacht

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Cacht of the Cultas Críamoine, who looks forty: a Hibernian-born maga raised at Qui Sonant and chosen by the Path of Strife. Turning from her House's usual morality drew her to conflict, and the siege offered a rare test, the overthrow of the way things were. She killed for Ballack, then lost interest in his goals.

She has no cause of her own and stays at Praesis only until one finds her, but she listens closely to Guillaume's reports on Connacht, scenting a new war in the making.

characters.name: Oscar von Harz
characters.summary: The guardian of the Gáe Bulg: a white-haired giant-blooded man, without fear and wholly loyal to Ballack, who stands on a wooden platform facing Meath with the spear held out as a challenge to any who would steal it. The book prints no stats for him.

characters.name: Meadhbh

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 120 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary:
The fallen leader of Praesis, now in sanctuary at Qui Sonant Pro Quieto, whose lands the Treaty makes a haven for all. When Holzner stole the Gáe Bulg she had him caught and executed and hung his head by its hair from the palisade; she held Praesis through a year's siege until Báetáin gave the spear away for her safe passage. Her druid allies had already left her, saying her demands had grown unreasonable. At Praesis they meet weekly to guess where she and her supporters are and whether they will come back.

The book gives neither her House (Ex Miscellanea is assumed) nor her age.

characters.name: Cú Chonnacht Cluasach Mac Tire

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 90 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: An independent Bjornaer magus, a vagrant at law: he belongs to no covenant, so he has no vote, no Redcap calls on him and nothing he owns is protected by the Code. He is famous for the Wizard War between him and Gráinne inghean Uaitéar of Vigil, which has never ended though the two have met face to face many times, the Tribunal's best example of a War that runs on until someone dies, yields or makes a treaty.
characters.secrets: The book says nothing more of him. His heartbeast is assumed to be a wolf, from his name (mac tíre is Irish for a wolf, and cluasach means big-eared).

characters.name: Peter

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 70 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: A Verditius stonemason who once worked at Qui Sonant beside Lewis. They fell out over Ingasia's claim to be Verditius's domus magna; when Finn took Lewis's side, Peter left, and he now wanders, nursing a vendetta he is about to escalate. He may exploit Lewis's warnings to rivals over one of the Coill Trí's Gifted children. Without a covenant he is a vagrant in Hibernian law. The book gives no age.

characters.name: Bressal Ua Boniségeas

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 60 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Bressal of Bonisagus, who has studied the peat moor of Beaghmore at length and holds that its warring auras are a shattered regio, broken by design or by accident. The book names no covenant for him and gives no age.

characters.name: Faolán

description.biography: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 35 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: A magus of the Younger House (Ex Miscellanea) who fled into Connacht before Praesis fell and has stayed far longer than three nights, a plain breach of the Treaty. His parens was one of the true Ollamhain, and he has only a weak grasp of the Hermetic Arts, so he feels nearer the Connacht druids than the Order; he may have friends among the Coill Trí. He belongs to no covenant, a vagrant at law.
characters.secrets: He is turning his back on the Order. The Tribunal has not yet worked out where he is; when it does, it will want him brought back, with or without the Coill Trí's help.

books.name: The library of Circulus Ruber
books.description: No books are named. The covenant honours Hermetic scholarship and invention; what it holds is not described.

books.name: The library of Cliffheart
books.description: No books are named. Kept disorderly on purpose, like the rest of the ráth, to keep faeries away. Palantus's records of faeries made to speak their true tongue are his research material, each usable once.

books.name: The library of Elk's Run
books.description:
No single book is named but the Ars Notoria, which Oswald learnt at Armagh. A very large collection in a stone scriptorium, with every room of Oswald's tower full of books besides: a superb library of mundane works, a fine set of Laboratory Texts and some rare magical volumes, gathered by copying at Armagh and trading with monasteries across Hibernia.

The Cow and Calf rule holds: a copy may be made, but leaves only in exchange for a text of equal value. Oswald hopes one day to give the rarest to Durenmar.

books.name: The Red Book of Cloyne
books.author: Imag and the leaders of Leth Moga after her
books.description:
The annals of the Order in Hibernia since 898, kept by Leth Moga's Redcaps from their own eye-witness accounts: Imag began it, Fergal mac Cuircc recorded the Schism War in it and then closed it to all but Redcaps, and Gopstan has spent many hours entering recent events. It also keeps old Irish lore, such as the tale of Eoghan Mór carried off alive from Magh Léana.

Diarmait holds it as his own property under his sanctum marker, by a ruling of the Tribunal; he will not have it copied but would like it to be seen. It is kept in the House's scriptorium, which has few defences. The book gives it no level or quality.

books.name: The library of Ashenrise
books.description: No books are named. Helles spends his days studying and glossing Hermetic law against the charges brought at each Tribunal, and the magi brought their texts from Normandy and Stonehenge; Pollices keeps notes and samples from every plague site in Ireland.

books.name: The texts of Lámbaird
books.description: Lámbaird keeps no library: each text stays with whichever magus used it last. Among them are the School of Raghallach's spells and its two Perdo Vim guidelines for dispelling Form and Realm resistance.

books.name: The library of the Paruchia
books.description: No books are named. It is kept in a tall tower on Little Saltee, and holds what the hermits need for Holy Magic and their devotions; Indrechtach adds to it by copying books at other covenants with their leave.

books.name: The library of Leth Cuinn
books.description: The book names no books and describes no library. What Leth Cuinn keeps is the clesrada, taught in person by Úathach through Initiation, and its Redcaps' knowledge of the northern High Roads.

books.name: The library of Qui Sonant
books.description: The book names no books. There are libraries in the manor, and an inner library of lab texts and casting tablets for the covenant's funerary rites and summonings, closely guarded and never shown to visitors. Finn Mac Cantarus writes Vitae Magorum in Irish, lives of magi much read across Hibernia, and the covenant researches the magi it has buried.

books.name: The drowned vaults of Vigil
books.description: The book names no books. Vigil's old library lies dark and untouched in the waterlogged vaults under the abandoned fortress: casting tablets and lab texts against Infernal sickness and harsh weather, with books and records earlier loremasters left to decay. Máel-ruanaid, its loremaster, takes the trust more seriously than they did. References to it survive in Hermetic annals and Vitae Magorum.

books.name: The library of Praesis
books.description: The book names no books at Praesis. What the old covenant kept from its centuries of dealings with Connacht's druids may have burned in the siege or gone with Meadhbh; the new masters have brought little, and Ballack is too poor to buy.

creatures.name: Fíorláir, the True Mare
creatures.how_many: a rare kind; each is a mare's seventh filly in a row

powers.name: Break the Hex
powers.description: Ends a spell that is on her if she can double its level on a stress die + 55. PeVi 40, a Greater Power.

powers.name: Born in the Saddle
powers.description: Whoever rides her adds +3 to Ride rolls. MuCo 5, a Lesser Power.

powers.name: Ward the Rider
powers.description: Her rider gains +5 Soak. She may keep it up as long as she likes, but regains the Might only once she lets it lapse, and each use gives the rider a Warping Point. MuCo 40, a Greater Power.

creatures.appearance: A horse of flawless build, caramel-coloured, with a mane and tail of cream.
creatures.notes:
When a mare foals seven fillies with no colt between them, the seventh may be a true mare. Nothing ill-meaning can touch her, her rider is kept from harm, and no horse can outrun her. Her Essential Trait, Swift as the Wind, adds +3 to running and jumping and stands in for her Quickness in any race. The magi of Lámbaird have tried to breed one and failed so far. A magus must win her friendship: binding one by magic brings the Eagle King's complaint at Tribunal, and a fíorláir once spoke for the beasts of magic there until an English magus asked her to be his familiar and she gave up the seat. Some of the old royal horses' descendants roaming near Armagh turn out to be true mares.
Where she first touched the earth at her birth grows seamair Mhuire, Mary's Clover, a four-leaved shamrock. Enriched (Realms of Power: Magic), set in silver, blessed by a priest and sung over to the Virgin daily for a season, it gives its wearer the Luck Virtue. Wound ranges: Light 1-7, Medium to 14, Heavy to 21, Incapacitated to 28, Dead from 29.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 10

creatures.name: Dobhar-chú, the King Otter
creatures.how_many: usually a mated pair, one hiding while the other fights

powers.name: Death Curse
powers.description: Falls at once on whoever deals it the killing blow, with +5 Penetration for each Fatigue level it had left (its Life Boost). Within a day the killer meets some deadly mishap, a falling bridge, a fire, a lightning stroke, which luck or skill may still let him survive. Counts as a level 50 spell for countering; a Ritual Power with no Hermetic equivalent.

vis.where: in the fur that bears the cross

creatures.appearance: An otter grown to seven feet from nose to tail, white all over save its black ears and a black stripe running down its back and across its shoulders in the shape of a cross.
creatures.notes:
Fierce as any lion, and proof against ordinary steel: only silver wounds it (its Lesser Malediction), and its Soak counts against any other metal as immunity. Its Combat totals include Ways of the Lough. It goes for the legs and hauls its prey toward the water; each round the grapple holds brings the victim nearer, and once in the water he must make a Deprivation roll every round he struggles. It is canny and often spends Fatigue to exert itself.
Its cross-marked skin is a famous charm, freed by Enrichment (Realms of Power: Magic), but only by the one who killed it and lived through the curse. Cured in salt, in smoke or in sweat, renewed and rubbed nine times nine times nine every day for a season, a scrap gives a ship Greater Immunity to Water, a house Greater Immunity to Fire, or a man Charmed Life (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages). The ship and the house are kept safe, not always the people in them. Wound ranges: Light 1-6, Medium to 12, Heavy to 18, Incapacitated to 24, Dead from 25.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 10

creatures.name: Bóinn, the Great White Cow

powers.name: Spirit Away
powers.description: A variable cost: adds Threshold points to those a mortal or a group has gathered (Realms of Power: Faerie).

powers.name: Allure
powers.description: +3 to Communication rolls to seduce.

powers.name: Appear Human
powers.description: Always on: she seems a lovely noblewoman, but hurt in the eye, the arm and the foot, wounds from gazing into the Well of Wisdom that will never heal. The book gives no Init.

powers.name: Deluge of Rushing and Dashing
powers.description: The Hermetic spell, but only on the Boyne; she drowns those who betrayed her as they ford it.

powers.name: Drowned Standing
powers.description: Fills the target's lungs with Boyne water for +15 damage that armour cannot soak.

powers.name: Guide
powers.description: Quietly steers a group toward deeds that help Meath at Leinster's cost, above all those that move wealth, power or office into Meath; the storyguide advises them as with Common Sense, but to her ends (Realms of Power: Faerie).

creatures.appearance: A huge white cow that shines, plainly more than a beast.
creatures.notes: A river goddess of the Tuatha Dé and wife of Nuadha, who sleeps under Sídh Neachtain at Carbury. Long ago she came to the Well of Wisdom, the spring at the Boyne's source, and it burst out in the flood that made the river. Her infidelity gave the Daghda a son, Aonghus, and she and Nuadha quarrel still. Where Nuadha stands for the kings of Leinster, she likes stories of power and riches flowing into Meath, as her river does: the Boroimhe tribute, or the justiciarship passing from FitzHenry to de Lacy, and she would rather her husband served than ruled. Pretenses are her Abilities here. Her Pretentious Quality concerns the rulers of Meath. The book prints Medium wounds to 13 and Incapacitated from 21, which do not fit Size +2; the ranges below are the standard ones. Wound ranges: Light 1-7, Medium to 14, Heavy to 21, Incapacitated to 28, Dead from 29.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 6

creatures.name: Donn, the Dark One

params.ward: a red ribbon tied in the hair or to a tail

powers.name: Create the Dead Host
powers.description: Makes a corpse that is the exact likeness of any man or woman he can see. Base 5, +1 Touch, +3 Moon.

powers.name: Bursting the Heart Vessel
powers.description: At his touch the victim's heart bursts and he dies on the spot. Base 30, +1 Touch, the spare Greater Power levels lowering its cost.

powers.name: Summon the Curtains of Donn
powers.description: Fog pours from his fingertip into a bank a mile across, which then behaves as any fog; he hides his comings and goings in it. Built as Base 2 with +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 Group, +1 size and +1 for being somewhat unnatural.

powers.name: Transform into Animal
powers.description: Takes the shape of a fish, a bull, a stag, a hawk or a boar, most often to fight his faerie foe Find. Base 10, +2 Sun, +1 size.

vis.where: one in each severed head tied to his belt

creatures.equipment: A warrior's arms and gear, and a chariot drawn by four horses.
creatures.appearance: Seven feet tall and bare but for a broad leather belt over his belly, from which ten human heads hang; blue tattoos cover his chest, arms and legs. A great spear fills his left hand and a sword his right, both forever dripping blood.
creatures.notes: The death god of the Tuatha Dé, a king like any other with sons, herds and raids on his neighbours. The dead gather at his rocky island palace, Teach Duínn, off the Munster coast. In war his three red-haired sons ride through the land spreading dread, and the slain are said to rise at Teach Duínn to march in his host; in peace he adds to it a man at a time, killing sleepers so their spirits fly to him, or leaving a false corpse behind and carrying the living man off. He fought the Order in the Schism War and hates the smith Goibhniu. Within Teach Duínn he keeps things that command the dead, walking corpse and ghost alike. A storyguide character, not balanced: his age and long study of men give him more Pretenses than the rules allow; they are his Abilities here. Good for feud stories, since his enemies are many, and for war. Wound ranges: Light 1-6, Medium to 12, Heavy to 18, Incapacitated to 24, Dead from 25.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 11
creatures.secrets: No one knows why he gathers an army. His great warded regio could hide one, and magi fear the endless fighting in Munster may set off another war with him; anyone starting a war with the Order would find him a ready ally. Nor is it known what the living captives are for: servants, husbands for his daughters, or subjects for his druids' tests.

creatures.name: Trooping Faerie
creatures.how_many: a troop of about twenty, each like the rest

params.ward: a bowl or a drop of fresh cow's milk

powers.name: Flight
powers.description: It flies, steering hard turns with Athletics. Base 4, +2 Sun.

powers.name: Invisibility
powers.description: It turns invisible. Base 4, +2 Sun, +1 moving image.

creatures.appearance: This troop are cat-folk: nearly a man's height, with a cat's face and ears and dangerous clawed hands, ragged clothes, and a leaping, bounding gait through the woods. Other troops look like ghostly copies of today's soldiers, stooped and hooded clansmen of old, or phantoms flying through the air.
creatures.notes: The slua sí: roving night gangs that wreck and sometimes kill along their path. They have played the part so long it is a story of its own, though some echo the fianna, Ostman raiders or the English knights now seizing what they can; the flying ones are taken for the restless dead, but have nothing to do with the Infernal or the Divine. One alone has no name and, questioned, can only repeat what its troop cares about. A single one is no great danger; together they kill. It fights in a trained group of its fellows as leader and vanguard, always adding the group bonus to its Attack. They do not parley beyond threats, other faeries use them as a menace or turn them on rivals, and their wanderings drive other faeries from their homes. A horse skull buried under a house, or a hearth kept lit all year, keeps them out. Lay brothers at Mellifont's grange near Newgrange have watched them ruin the crops. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 11

creatures.name: Caílte mac Rónáin

powers.name: Speech of the Deer
powers.description: He talks with an animal within reach of his voice. Base 10, +2 Voice, +1 Conc.

powers.name: Speed of the Deer
powers.description: He runs as fast as a deer, +3 to rolls for racing or speed. Base 15, +2 Sun.

powers.name: Removal of a Thousand Cares
powers.description: Like Pains of the Thousand Worries without the pain: the target turns idle and listless from joy. He often uses it when a tale is done, to prove he belongs among Ireland's poets, but needs no poem to use it. Base 4, +2 Voice, +3 Moon, +1 complex; four spare levels bring the cost to 0.

vis.where: in four strands of his golden hair

creatures.equipment: A spear, a sword, and the old dress of an Irish noble.
creatures.appearance: A fine-looking youth, long and straight of limb, with flowing golden hair, in the clothes of a far older age: a patterned cloak flung over one shoulder and pinned with a rich brooch.
creatures.notes: Fionn mac Cumhaill's nephew, a poet and warrior from the Tales of the Elders, who guided Saint Patrick's company across Munster telling him Fionn's stories. He believes the saint raised him from the dead, and now he roams Ireland's fields and woods as a man. Though incognizant, he can raise his Pretenses, which are his Abilities here. He is baptised and a true Christian, though Dominion auras weaken his powers. He leads a band he calls fianna and tries to keep them to noble deeds, but they mostly rob and plunder as they please. The book builds him as a companion a player could run. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 11
creatures.secrets: His fianna are outlaws who have gone over to the faerie.

creatures.name: The Head of Arastotail

powers.name: The Master's Agreement
powers.description: Brings a man round to agree with whatever case the head has put. MuMe Base 15, +2 Voice, +2 Sun.

powers.name: Trust of the Master's Servant
powers.description: Like Trust of Childlike Faith: makes the target trust him, if someone holds the head and the target meets its eyes. PeMe Base 4, +1 Eye, +2 Sun.

powers.name: Master of Waves
powers.description: Any Intellego, Rego, Muto or Perdo Aquam effect of level 25 or less, costing a Might Point a magnitude.

creatures.appearance: A Greek scholar's head, hook-nosed, with wiry hair going thin on top; the neck ends in a stump of skin, with no blood.
creatures.notes: The Irish hold Aristotle to have been a magician, Arastotail, whose wife foiled his study of bees, stars and tides and beat him in every quarrel. Seeking to live for ever, he cut off his own head and bade a servant bury it in a certain spot and dig it up at dawn. In some tellings the servant forgot and the magician died; in others the head's muffled shouts carried far from the mound, until a farmer unearthed it and it ordered him to go and find its body. It loves to order men about on lowly errands to prove itself their better, a feeble proof, and now and then enjoys a learned dispute on philosophy. Women are beyond its power, and near one it grows slow and foolish. Its Pretenses are its Abilities here. Wound ranges: Light 1-2, Medium to 4, Heavy to 6, Incapacitated to 8, Dead from 9.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 11

creatures.name: Harvest Thief
creatures.how_many: hundreds, loosed on the fields together
creatures.weakness: Abhorrent Material (the sound of a barking dog)

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Takes on a body, which it must do to gnaw through the crops.

powers.name: The Thief of Vitality
powers.description: Kills one plant of a grain or root crop, or one fruit in an orchard.

creatures.appearance: Unseen and bodiless, it rides a breeze that runs through the crops against the wind. Given a body it is a skinny green imp the size of a wheat grain, with absurdly long limbs, long ears that thin to a trailing thread, and sharp crooked teeth for chewing through crops, which sets off its power.
creatures.notes: One of Hibernia's many demons of hardship, each with a little power over some disaster. Each has a taste for one crop and cannot bear any other, and they are seldom found abroad outside the harvest. Timid and easily kept off, by magic or by a dog's barking, which terrifies them. A swarm can be boiled down to a single pawn of tainted vis, Vis Infesta (Realms of Power: The Infernal). Any wound kills one. Like every demon of Ireland since Saint Patrick, it may not take a serpent's shape.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 13

creatures.name: The Sluagh
creatures.how_many: a flock, gathering wherever a death is near
creatures.weakness: Compulsiveness (may enter a house only by an open window facing west)

powers.name: Let Me In
powers.description: Though bodiless, it can rattle shut doors and shutters, and does so at any west window barred against it.

powers.name: Come With Me
powers.description: Pulls the dying target's last breath, and his spirit with it. If it gets the spirit a mile off, the spirit becomes a Sluagh too; if it loses hold, another may pay the Might and try again.

creatures.appearance: Starved grey things with long thin hair trailing from torn and clawed scalps, lips pulled so far back the whole jaw shows, and blind, lidless eyes. They fly with their rags streaming as if dragged through water.
creatures.notes: Invisible spirits that scent death coming and flock to the dying from the west, keening as they fly and falling silent at the house. In they climb by the window, to crouch on every surface with teeth softly clicking, or knock at shutters closed against them. One seizes the last breath and drags the spirit out, and the flock flees shrieking, flaying it until it is gaunt and lidless like them. They have no hold on a spirit that dies before they get in, or that has had Extreme Unction. Closing the west windows, which an Intelligence + Infernal Lore roll against 6 reveals, keeps them out, and Nightwalkers (Hedge Magic) gather on a night a death is expected to guard the soul. Blind but sharp of hearing: under the magical combat rules of Houses of Hermes: Societates every foe is Indistinct to them (+3 Attack and +6 Defense for the foe), except when grappling. They travel together but always fight as an untrained group, and leave damp patches where they took a victim, from their slavering. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 13

creatures.name: Temoneth, Messenger of Delgnat's Betrayal
creatures.weakness: Protected Group (those truly happy in marriage)

powers.name: Berserker Rage
powers.description: Grants anyone the Berserk Virtue until they calm down.

powers.name: The Betrayal Revealed
powers.description: Once the target has brought himself to the edge of suspicion, makes him wholly certain of it.

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: The usual demonic power.

powers.name: Endurance of the Enraged
powers.description: She suffers no wound penalties save to Defense.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: The usual demonic power; her sin is lust.

powers.name: Possession
powers.description: The usual demonic power, at a variable cost.

powers.name: Waxing Tide of Humors
powers.description: Passion swamps reason: the victim needs a stress roll against 9, adjusted by fitting Personality Traits, to master an anger, lust, wantonness or spite. She often follows a successful Obsession with it.

creatures.appearance: From the front a voluptuous naked woman with only a scrap of veil over her face. When she turns, a ragged line of flesh has been torn away to bare the bloody skeleton, her bowels dangle from the back of her open pelvis, and her heel bones click wetly as she walks.
creatures.notes: The child of greed and deceit, behind many of Ireland's woes since Delgnat betrayed her husband Partholon, among them the flight of Dervorgilla, the Uí Ruairc queen, with her husband's sworn enemy Dermot MacMurrough. She sows lust and strife between men and women, but is too proud to trouble the lowly when their betters offer better sport. The book prints her Area Lore without a score and a stray 9 after Brawl; the 9 is taken as the Area Lore's. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 13
creatures.secrets: Her chief weapon is Possession: she hides in the courts of the rich, preferably in several advisers to the main players at once, and urges reckless deeds dressed as wise counsel, stirring lust for what cannot be had until betrayal and cruel revenge follow. But she has no self-control: an insult to one of her hosts can drive her to murder, wrecking her schemes and forcing her to flee before she is found out.

creatures.name: Saint Patrick (St. Pátraig)

powers.name: Shatter Idol
powers.description: A curse that crumbles a false stone idol lately worshipped into rubble.

powers.name: The Captive Made Free
powers.description: The ground shakes, prison walls crack, doors fly open and chains drop from captives or slaves.

powers.name: The Unquenchable Fire
powers.description: A blessed hearth fire that never goes out, even with no fuel left; fires lit from it are ordinary.

powers.name: The Sky Made Light
powers.description: By day, clears away storm, cloud or magical foul weather until sunset.

creatures.notes:
Born in Britain, he converted Ireland (his life is in the history). His best-known miracle cast every snake and venomous creature out of the island for ever, and no demon of Ireland may now take a serpent's form. Anyone born Irish may call on him, as on Brigid and Columba. His Latin name is Patricius; the name he bore in life, Cothraige, is forgotten by 1220.

Venerated in all Ireland; patron of Ireland. Feast: 17 March.

Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Apparition, Expel Demons, Resist Temptation (St. Patrick's Breastplate), Scourging of Snakes, The Faithful Made Whole.

Irish saints are said to take a close interest in the doings of magicians, and the Meddlesome Saint Hook (Covenants) suits a saga here.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 12

creatures.name: Saint Brigid of Kildare (Naomh Bríd)

powers.name: Call Forth the Waters
powers.description: Raises a wave fifty paces wide and ten high that can sweep a small island bare; or, more kindly, opens a spring of fresh water.

powers.name: Counting Sheep
powers.description: A flock or herd that was lost, or given to the poor, is found to be whole again when counted.

powers.name: Test of Truth
powers.description: A curse: until the petitioner has done questioning him, the victim can speak only truth, and an attempt to lie throws him down in fits. He may keep silent; even demons cannot lie under it.

creatures.notes:
Also called Brigit, or Mary of the Gael. Daughter of a nobleman and a concubine sold, while carrying her, to a magician, she was so holy as a baby that she would not eat his food and lived on cows' milk. Vowed to lifelong virginity, she became a nun, though some say the blind bishop who received her vows made her a bishop by mistake, and saw again as he finished. She drove her chariot across Ireland healing, preaching and helping the poor, for whom she had a special love. Her Sacred Fire burns at Kildare.

Venerated in all Ireland; patron of Ireland, with Patrick and Columba. Feast: 1 February.

Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Apparition, Cure Blindness, Expel Demons, Resist Temptation, Sanctuary of Virginity, The Faithful Made Whole, Tomorrow's Bounty.

Irish saints are said to take a close interest in the doings of magicians, and the Meddlesome Saint Hook (Covenants) suits a saga here.
creatures.source: The Contested Isle: The Hibernian Tribunal ch. 12

creatures.name: Saint Columba (Saint Colum Cille)

powers.name: Banish Magical Monster
powers.description: Demon's Eternal Oblivion, but against Magic Animals: if it penetrates, the beast's Might falls for good by the saint's Might.

powers.name: Borne up by Angels
powers.description: One falling to his death who calls on the saint, if heard, is caught by angels (Divine Might 15) who slow the fall and set him down gently.

powers.name: Multitude of Fish
powers.description: Waters whose fish have dwindled or gone become a place fish flock to, enriching the local fisherfolk.

powers.name: Walk Upon the Waters
powers.description: The one blessed walks on waves or rivers as on stone, out to a boat and back again.

creatures.notes:
One of the twelve apostles of Ireland. He founded several monasteries, then copied a book in Saint Finian of Movilla's scriptorium and meant to keep the copy; Finian claimed it, the quarrel grew, and many died at the Battle of Cúl Dreimhne. Exiled for it, he went to convert the Picts, founded Iona, a house of great austerity, and banished the beast of Loch Ness, among many wonders.

Venerated in all Ireland, Kells and Derry; Scotland, above all Iona; patron of Ireland (with Patrick and Brigid), Derry, warriors, exiles, Scotland and Iona. Feast: 9 June.

Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Acknowledgment of Evil, Apparition, Dysentric Infliction, Expel Demons, Raise the Dead, Resist Temptation, The Dutiful Shepherd.

creatures.notes:
A prince of Leinster, unusual for having become a Christian before Patrick came, on travels in England. He converted some of the royal kin around Wexford, founded a monastery at Abingdon in England, banished a sea serpent on a voyage to see the Pope and saved his people from another monster at home. Loved as an Irishman who converted the English, he is the patron of those who resist English interference in the Irish Church. Ailbe Ua Mail Mhuaidh, Bishop of Ferns, wrote his life in 1218 and is spreading his cult.

Venerated in Leinster, above all Wexford and the diocese of Ferns; patron of those who would keep the Irish Church free of English meddling. Feast: 16 March.

Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Apparition.

powers.name: Protect the Wild Prey
powers.description: A wild beast the saint blesses scares off hounds and cannot be hurt by weapons until sunset.

powers.name: Strange Fruit
powers.description: Any tree bears good fruit, out of season the first time; it breeds true, and its offspring fruit in season after.

powers.name: Tame the Wild Beast
powers.description: Gives the petitioner one divine animal companion, which does not age while the petitioner lives and helps as a friend would; betray or harm it and the saint curses the petitioner.

creatures.notes:
A hermit of royal blood whose holiness drew followers; he fled them to a remote hill at Glendalough, and when they came anyway he founded a monastery there. Best known for making willows bear apples, he loved wild creatures, which often helped him. His name means the gentle one.

Venerated in Leinster; patron of Dublin, Glendalough and crows. Feast: 3 June.

Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Apparition, Raise the Dead.

powers.name: Bless the Book
powers.description: Water can no longer harm the blessed book, which stays readable even after centuries on a lough bed.

creatures.notes:
Ciarán the Younger, one of the twelve apostles of Ireland and a bishop, spent his youth herding in Connacht. A lover of learning, he founded many monasteries, the greatest Clonmacnoise, where the yellow plague of Justinian took him early in the sixth century. His cow gave the vellum of the Book of the Dun Cow.

Venerated in Meath, and Clonmacnoise; patron of herdsmen and cattle. Feast: 9 September.

Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Apparition, Resist Temptation, The Faithful Made Whole.

powers.name: Multitude of Fish

creatures.notes:
Archbishop of Armagh from 1132 to his death in 1148, in troubled times for the Irish Church; despite many plots he rose from post to post, helped by the miracles granted him. A great exorcist and a visionary, he brought fish back to empty rivers and bays and healed the sick. The Prophecy of the Popes said to be his lies lost in the Vatican, not to be found for centuries.

Venerated in Ulster, above all Armagh; patron of Armagh, visionaries and fisherfolk. Feast: 3 November.

Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Apparition, Expel Demons, The Faithful Made Whole, Rebuke the Unfaithful.

powers.name: Cure Madness

powers.name: Test of Truth

creatures.notes:
A king's daughter, only fifteen when she died. After her mother's death her father, who saw his wife in her, sought to marry her; she fled to Ghent, where his men killed her. Both the Irish and the Flemish mercenaries in English pay honour her. Her staff, her bachall, is kept at Tydavnet in Ulster and can tell truth from lies.

Venerated in Ulster and Flanders, above all Ghent; patron of Ghent, Tydavnet, the insane and the anxious. Feast: 15 May.

Other powers (Realms of Power: The Divine): Apparition, Grant of Serenity, Sanctuary of Virginity.

powers.name: Hide Fugitive
powers.description: The petitioner looks like a natural feature, and feels and sounds like one too, hiding her from pursuers.

powers.name: Still the Waves

creatures.notes:
Famed for his voyages to the western isles and the Isle of the Blessed, he was also an abbot, a founder of monasteries and a worker of wonders. Once he made a runaway slave look like a rock, and the rock like the slave, so the pursuers hauled off the stone. His relics are at Clonfert.

Venerated in Connacht, above all Ardfert, Inishdadroum, Clonfert and Annaghdown; patron of explorers, navigators, Clonfert and Ardfert. Feast: 16 May.

creatures.notes:
In his day the Fir Bolg warred with the tribe of Colla da Chrioch. They broke a first truce, seizing the king's son and killing him when their queen grew fond of him, and plotted to break a second; as they drew their weapons the saint, watching from his church, prayed, and the ground swallowed them. Some say they lie beneath the bog of Magh Liach still; others that they went straight to Hell.

Venerated in Connacht, above all Ballinasloe; patron of the betrayed, those threatened by the Fir Bolg, and Ballinasloe. Feast: 29 September.

Best known for driving off the Scathach, the sea serpent that ate anyone sailing near Scattery Island, with the sign of the Cross so he could found his monastery there; he overcame many more monsters by prayer and cursed many bandits to death. Women were barred from his island: he buried his beloved sister, Saint Ibie, between the tide marks rather than on it, and another woman died in her boat on the shore after years of waiting to be let land.

Venerated in Munster; patron of Scattery Island, the Corco Baiscinn and the Uí Fhidgeinte. Feast: 8 March.
