c_chonnacht_cluasach_mac_tire.name: Cú Chonnacht Cluasach Mac Tire

description.biography: Feud: Gráinne inghean Uaitéar of Vigil, in a Wizard War that has never been ended, however often they have met.

c_chonnacht_cluasach_mac_tire.summary: An independent Bjornaer magus, a vagrant at law: he belongs to no covenant, so he has no vote, no Redcap calls on him and nothing he owns is protected by the Code. He is famous for the Wizard War between him and Gráinne inghean Uaitéar of Vigil, which has never ended though the two have met face to face many times, the Tribunal's best example of a War that runs on until someone dies, yields or makes a treaty.
c_chonnacht_cluasach_mac_tire.secrets: The book says nothing more of him. His heartbeast is assumed to be a wolf, from his name (mac tíre is Irish for a wolf, and cluasach means big-eared).

milvia.name: Milvia
milvia.summary:
Praeco of Hibernia, looking sixty-eight. She is not the eldest magus of the Tribunal, but Conán Derg gave up the office. Her passion is political unity, and she has steered a turbulent Tribunal skilfully through most of its storms; she has been Praeco at the last four meetings and led Hibernia's delegation to the Grand Tribunal of 1195.

As a Bonisagus she respects Cliffheart's original research, though she fears its success would harm Hibernia's unity. She takes no side between the Irish and English magi.

visioturpis.name: Visioturpis
visioturpis.summary:
Hibernia's oldest Quaesitor and its presiding Quaesitor, looking fifty-six: ugly, bent and irritable, his long face scarred down both sides and his greasy hair hanging in strands. His name joins the Latin for face and ugly.

Painful Magic makes him slow to cast, so he prefers one mighty spell to several small ones, though such spells flood him with more than he can sort and details get lost. He has reversed his rulings when what he first learned proved false; he is no fool to cling to a bad judgement, but he remembers long and hates to be shown wrong.

con_n_derg.name: Conán Derg
con_n_derg.summary:
The oldest magus in Hibernia, who looks a hale twenty-nine and says his strong faerie blood keeps him young. He was Praeco when the trouble between Irish and English magi began and stood by the Peripheral Code, insisting that all the newcomers wanted could be had under it; in 1186 he accepted Ashenrise's cathach.

Two months after the meeting of 1186, wandering alone on the Connacht border, he was ambushed and his right arm was taken off at the shoulder. He would not let magic regrow it: by the old Irish belief that a leader must be whole, he gave up the office of Praeco and withdrew from Hermetic politics, and he has seemed happier ever since. Some suspect Faisgia of Cliffheart; Conán Derg neither denies nor confirms it.

faisgia.name: Faisgia
faisgia.summary:
Cliffheart's leader, filius of one of its founders, looking ninety-eight. He spends most of his time roaming Munster for faeries who fought in the Schism War. He keeps the cathach: each year he casts the spell that holds the Diedne magus in stone, and he works the Rego Terram magic that carries it to every Tribunal.

Since Conán Derg was maimed on ground Faisgia often travels, some magi suspect him of the ambush; he scoffs at the idea.

ruaidr_m_r.name: Ruaidrí Mór
ruaidr_m_r.summary: A Merinita of Cliffheart who specialises in Rego and travels the Tribunal studying faeries. The book gives no more of him.

ine_dhubh.name: Áine Dhubh
ine_dhubh.summary: Black Ann, a Merinita of Cliffheart who specialises in Herbam and travels the Tribunal studying faeries. The book gives no more of her.

coscrach_cam.name: Coscrach Cam
coscrach_cam.summary: A combative Merinita of Cliffheart who travels the Tribunal among the faeries. The book gives no more of him.

palantus.name: Palantus
palantus.summary:
A German magus trained in the Rhine, looking forty-three, and a born linguist, researching how to cast spells in Irish. He has made a spell that compels a faerie to talk in its old, truer tongue instead of its Faerie Speech Pretense, records what it says and builds his research on it; each interview serves only once.

He longs to meet and talk with every new faerie, but is ill at ease away from a laboratory and his sodales want no faerie visitors, so he often asks other Hibernian magi to lend him their laboratories for his interviews.

styrbj_rn.name: Styrbjórn
styrbj_rn.summary: A Scandinavian born in Dublin and trained at Verdi, looking fifty-five. He came home to guard his family when he heard of the English invasion, found they were in no real danger, and discovered he loved his homeland; Cliffheart took him in. He lives at the back of the ráth making magic items for his sodales, and gladly takes commissions from other Irish magi.

oswald.name: Oswald
oswald.summary:
Founder and leader of Elk's Run, looking seventy: a tiny man, scarcely a boy's size, under a shock of untidy white hair. Born in Leinster to an Irish mother, he was carried off to Stonehenge in childhood and brought up there, and after his Gauntlet planned his return, befriending Lugardis.

His adventures are long behind him. He is wholly given to a rebirth of learning in Hibernia and to saving the island's texts for posterity: collecting, copying and trading books. Gentle Gifted, he has many friends among Irish and English nobles and clerics. He trusts to cunning and trickery against his enemies, whom he takes to be jealous of his standing in House Bonisagus and the Order abroad, and means one day to give his rarest texts to Durenmar.

He is teaching two apprentices at once, which takes half his time; once they pass their Gauntlets he may leave Ireland with the library if the politics turn bad.

lugardis.name: Lugardis
lugardis.summary:
An Italian Quaesitor with raven hair, sharp features and a piercing stare, looking sixty-four, who has served in four Tribunals; she came from the Rhine, sent by Durenmar to look into the state of the Order in Hibernia after English magi wrote to Magvillus and Durenmar of hostility and barbarous customs and demanded reform. Her Blatant Gift frightens covenfolk and Irish folk, who cross themselves as she goes by, and sours milk almost at once, so she keeps away from the cattle and the dairy.

She has come to see that Hibernia keeps the Code, if with an odd Peripheral Code, and having read Oswald's books she is amused by the Stonehenge magi's fear that Connacht shelters the last of the Diedne. Her letters home and to Durenmar explain the local customs and praise the Irish Order, who still suspect her deeply. She wants a diplomatic answer to the covenant's troubles, is appalled by Igneous and worried by Oswald.

igneous_drake.name: Igneous Drake
igneous_drake.summary:
A Stonehenge magus, looking seventy-two, in Hibernia only ten years: he came because he heard English magi were persecuted here, and because the macgnímartha raiders let him test his magic on the Hermetically trained, a better fight than hedge wizards. Violent, scornful of the natives and their ways, he delights in conflict and in burning the covenant's enemies.

He has made a spell that raises a wall of fire on a Boundary, ringing the covenant during a raid; he burns those trapped inside and then hunts the survivors down. Bored of waiting for attacks, he has begun Wizard Wars against Irish magi. He backed the Siege of Praesis eagerly, spending seasons there teaching the attackers Ignem spells and doing much to bring the island covenant down, and he is a firm friend of Ballack and the new Praesis.

diarmait_mac_fergaile.name: Diarmait mac Fergaile
diarmait_mac_fergaile.summary:
Leader of Leth Moga, an un-Gifted Redcap who looks seventy-five, and Fergal's son-in-law, who took over when his parens Fergal died; the Red Book came to him from Fergal as his own property. Unlike Fergal he thinks opening the Red Book to readers would add to its worth: it must not be copied, but it should be seen.

The other Redcaps care more about whom he will name to follow him, Gopstan or Luathan. Dáire Cú of Leth Cuinn thinks him too doddering and bookish to lead the Tribunal's Redcaps.

gopstan_mac_diarmata.name: Gopstan mac Diarmata
gopstan_mac_diarmata.summary:
Diarmait's filius and son-in-law, looking thirty-seven, who has never left Ireland; his name comes from Irish slang for 'Poor John'. Born rich, he gave away his goods with a show when he passed his Gauntlet. He was apprenticed late and knows House Mercere's ways less well than Redcaps of his age, which weighs on Diarmait when he thinks of handing over the House.

He loves the Red Book dearly and has spent hours writing recent events into it. He once spent a year at Cashel posing as an unlettered prince's son to read its library, and was found out.

ercc_cam.name: Ercc Cam
ercc_cam.summary: A Redcap of Leth Moga, un-Gifted like all its Redcaps, who trained his nephew Luathan as his filius. The book gives no more of him.

luathan.name: Luathan
luathan.summary:
Ercc Cam's filius and nephew, dashing and handsome and the best-loved Redcap of the south. He has the temper for the Cult of Heroes, but when he took his uncle's offer to train him his angry mother laid a geas on him, 'forever mundane or forever lame', so he may learn no Virtue that would give him quasi-magical powers; barred from the initiations of Leth Cuinn, he stayed south of the Eiscir Riada.

He makes good use of magic items instead: a cloak that turns him into an eagle and a harpoon that lets him breathe under water.

r_n_n.name: Rónán
r_n_n.summary: A weepy Redcap of Leth Moga, parens of Áine. The book gives no more of him.

ine.name: Áine
ine.summary: A Redcap of Leth Moga, Rónán's filia. The book gives no more of her.

helles.name: Helles
helles.summary:
Founder and leader of Ashenrise, looking thirty-seven. Born in Champagne and trained in the Normandy Tribunal, he joined Moles Magna because a covenant inside a dam seemed a good place to hide from the world; when the dam burst and swept it away, he chose to hide in plain sight instead, and his grog captain Ralph fitz Stephen brought him to his kin in Ireland.

A master of disputation in both the schoolmen's manner and his House's, he sees rewriting Hibernia's Peripheral Code as the greatest challenge there is. He studies and glosses Hermetic law daily to answer the high crimes charged against him and his sodales at every meeting.

links.note: Fellow founder; fled Moles Magna with him

pollices.name: Pollices
pollices.summary:
'Thumbs', a founder of Ashenrise, looking forty-two: tall, hawk-like and dressed in black, a Sicilian with four thumbs, two where his little fingers should be, from an accident in his apprenticeship. No lover of beauty, he studies deformity and deadly plague, and has visited every place in Ireland where plague killed a crowd, gathering samples of something few can name. Irish magi find him grim and frightening.

Among mundanes he is another man: his Gentle Gift lets him pass as a gloved scholar and physician of many languages, charming and pleasant, a welcome guest at the neighbouring lords' courts and much loved by the English settlers.

dyfrgi.name: Dyfrgi
dyfrgi.summary: A Welsh magus of House Bjornaer with a wolf heartbeast, one of the three founders of Ashenrise who remain. The book says no more of him.

tug.name: Tug
tug.summary: Once Decamentus, a faithful follower of his House's ways, he met Saint Patrick in a long Temporary Twilight, and the saint blessed the coarse blanket he had wrapped himself in against the cold. He chose a new life at once, came to Hibernia and renamed himself Tug, which is a shawl in Irish slang. No covenant but Ashenrise would take him. Looks thirty-eight.

dorj_n.name: Dorján
dorj_n.summary: Born and trained in the Transylvanian Tribunal and sent on to Stonehenge, he and Konstanczia asked leave to join the new Hibernian covenant and came too late to help defend its cathach. Handsome and charming, he would be Leinster's most eligible bachelor but for his Gift. Always the defender, he has fought half a dozen Wizard Wars in Hibernia and killed four magi. Looks forty-three.

links.note: Sodalis of House Tremere; came with him from Stonehenge

konstanczia.name: Konstanczia
konstanczia.summary: Dorján's elder and wiser companion from Transylvania by way of Stonehenge. She keeps her mind on Tribunal business and watches the known troublemakers. She too has fought half a dozen Wizard Wars as the defender, and has killed five magi. Looks forty-five.

dalton_ballaugh.name: Dalton Ballaugh

description.biography: Feud: Éinri mac Cillíni of Vigil, who has learned the cost of Dalton's fire in years of certamen and skirmishes between their grogs, short of Wizard War so far.

dalton_ballaugh.summary:
Dalton Ballaugh an Flámbó (DOLL-ton BOLL-odge), leader of Lámbaird, looking forty-three. His father was an Uí Broin, and the covenfolk still call him Mac ind Óc, the Young Son, though few of them are his elders. He and Brian were apprentices together and passed their Gauntlets together, and are close friends.

A great hunter, which shows in his Intellego: he reads a site as well as any Quaesitor. His mastery of fire matches it, and he is a dangerous enemy, as Éinri mac Cillíni of Vigil has learnt; the two have feuded for years, short of Wizard War. His familiar is Lóegaire Liath, Grey Lóegaire, a grizzled hunting dog, sire of the covenant's line of magical hounds.

links.note: Close friend; apprenticed and gauntleted together

brian_chilldara.name: Brian Chilldara
brian_chilldara.summary:
Brian of Cilldara an Flámbó, looking fifty-seven: small, thin and entirely hairless, a skinchanger who becomes a salmon and spends long spells in Wicklow's lakes and streams, studying the moods of the water he loves.

His familiar, a salmon like his other shape, was caught and eaten by Norman soldiers. He has not got over it and may never bind another; until then he means to destroy every Norman on Irish soil.

cliodna_inghean_hiolair.name: Cliodna inghean hIolair
cliodna_inghean_hiolair.summary: Cliodna an Flámbó (CLEE-na), the youngest at Lámbaird, looking thirty-five, who has made herself in the image of a warrior-queen of legend: as good with a sword as with a spell, a superb rider and athlete. She is called daughter of the Eagle since a clan of magical birds of prey in the mountains adopted her, and her familiar is Artt, a son of the Eagle King.

fedelmid.name: Fedelmid
fedelmid.summary:
Fedelmid an t-Éigse Measceal (FEDGE-el-midge on TCHAY-shuh MYES-kul), comarba Nerius, leader of the Paruchia, looking ninety-five. A young Céli Dé, he joined House Ex Miscellanea believing the Order the very spirit of learning and discipline a Gifted holy man should seek. Many of its members disappointed him; he stays loyal to his sodales but never puts them before the Church. His is not a loyalty to sees, bishops and institutions but a personal, heroic asceticism, a saint's life of his own.

His pilgrimage changed him twice over: the Alpine visions sent him in search of the few who knew Nerius's secret, and Rome taught him that the Pope has spiritual authority but that spiritual troubles are best mended locally by those they touch. He trained Indrechtach, and grieved when Glendalough cast him out.

Now very old, worn by decrepitude and long bouts of Twilight, he is preparing to leave Little Saltee to die and be buried at Qui Sonant Pro Quieto, and hopes the covenant's next visitors will escort him there.

links.note: His apprentice, trained in Holy Magic

c_emgen.name: Cóemgen
c_emgen.summary: Cóemgen an t-Éigse Measceal (COE-muh-gen), newly gauntleted, looking his age: a manaim, who keeps the hours but has not taken a monk's full vows and may marry. He longs to marry and raise a family on Great Saltee, crossing to the covenant each day, but there is no unwed woman on the island, and his Gift and crippling shyness spoil his hopes. Gentle and likeable, he may one day row to Wexford to carry off a bride, or court a woman he meets, earnestly and clumsily.

d_ire_c_ua_d_ire_ua_mearcaire.name: Dáire Cú Ua Dáire Ua Mearcaire
d_ire_c_ua_d_ire_ua_mearcaire.summary: The unGifted leader of Leth Cuinn, who looks sixty-three; he took the house from his father, Dáire Direach, and is shaping his eldest son, Dáire an Chogaidh, to follow him. He is ritually wed to Úathach, and since his mortal wife died the marriage has been more than a form. He has nothing but scorn for the Redcaps of Leth Moga, and thinks their leader too doddering and bookish to lead the Tribunal's Redcaps.

d_ire_an_chogaidh_mac_d_ire_c.name: Dáire an Chogaidh Mac Dáire Cú
d_ire_an_chogaidh_mac_d_ire_c.summary:
Dáire Cú's eldest son, an unGifted Redcap who looks forty-eight. In his macgnímartha he fought de Courcy's English with the army of Ulster, which is how he got his name, 'of the wars'. He is against everything English and has even voted at Tribunal, for all his House's custom of neutrality; it has made him something of a celebrity, and the primus of House Mercere is rumoured to be readying an answer.

He is more often on the drill ground with warriors than out on Ireland's roads, which is just where his father, well aware of his temper, wants him: a superb, frightening drill-master.

elen_bhodhar_inghean_d_ire_c_ua_mearcair.name: Elen Bhodhar inghean Dáire Cú Ua Mearcaire
elen_bhodhar_inghean_d_ire_c_ua_mearcair.summary: Elen the Deaf, youngest of Dáire Cú's five children, an unGifted Redcap of nineteen. Her mother died bearing her, and she was born without hearing; she reads lips perfectly and speaks through mime and a rough sign language. She has just finished her Redcap training and begun to ride Ireland's roads.

cantarus_an_t_iarbiteon.name: Cantarus an t-Iarbiteon
cantarus_an_t_iarbiteon.summary: Master of the Songs, the head of Qui Sonant, for fifty years without a challenger; a magus of Jerbiton who looks eighty-five, born in the covenant and seldom outside it since. He knows death or Twilight is not far off, but has found no heir to trust with the covenant: most of the apprentices he has trained have walked away from Qui Sonant's burden, and only Finn remains, who has the wish to lead but not the gift.

finn_mac_cantarus_an_t_iarbiteon.name: Finn Mac Cantarus an t-Iarbiteon
finn_mac_cantarus_an_t_iarbiteon.summary:
Cantarus's filius, of Jerbiton, who looks thirty-five. He has a gift for Vitae Magorum in Irish, and his histories of the Order are read all over Hibernia; he cares deeply for his covenant and the peace and fellowship it stands for.

He takes it for granted that, as Cantarus's only filius at the covenant, he will be the next Master of the Songs, and has no idea of his pater's doubts. So he learns nothing from his mistakes as a leader, talks freely of his coming rank, and buys friends with long-term promises on the strength of it. He took Lewis's side when the two Verditius quarrelled.

lewis_cultas_bh_ardaoiteas.name: Lewis Cultas Bhéardaoiteas

description.biography: Feud: Peter of Verditius, once Qui Sonant's second stonemason, who left when the two quarrelled over Ingasia's claim to be Verditius's domus magna and Finn sided with Lewis. Peter, now an exile on the roads, is about to escalate the vendetta, and would gladly exploit Lewis's warning-off of rivals for a Gifted child of the tithe.

lewis_cultas_bh_ardaoiteas.summary:
Master Stonemason of Qui Sonant, of Verditius, who looks fifty. There were two Verditius stonemasons here until they fell out over whether Ingasia may call itself Verditius's domus magna; to cool the quarrel Finn sided with Lewis, and Peter chose to leave. Lewis offers younger Verditius Initiation into the House Mysteries, but only if they declare for Verdi, and such Initiates may find themselves caught in the vendetta his exiled rival is about to widen.

He would pay well for an apprentice with a talent for craft magic, and within a few years will probably go to the Coill Trí seeking one of the seven Gifted children they owe each Tribunal; he will even warn rivals off the child, which Peter, now wandering, may turn against him.

turlough_cultas_cr_othamon.name: Turlough Cultas Críothamon
turlough_cultas_cr_othamon.summary: Turlough of Criamon, who looks fifty-five, governs the cemetery, the funeral rites and the protection of the spirits in the covenant's keeping, and is well thought of inside the covenant and out. His own magic is the summoning of spirits. He has trained one apprentice and won another at the last Tribunal through his warm relations with the Coill Trí.
turlough_cultas_cr_othamon.secrets: He feels there is more to gain from the spirits than summoning them, and fears his sodales will learn of this growing interest, so any help must come from outside; he would gladly bargain his influence with the Coill Trí for it.

inri_mac_cill_ni_mich_d_ire_boircech.name: Éinri mac Cillíni mich Dáire Boircech

description.biography: Feud: Dalton Ballaugh of Lámbaird. They have fought certamen after certamen and their grogs clash often; it is not yet Wizard War, but they loathe each other, perhaps because they and their covenants are so alike.

inri_mac_cill_ni_mich_d_ire_boircech.summary:
Vigil's leader, though not its eldest, a magus of Merinita who looks sixty: he keeps the bees, rules the herds and holds the black pig's tusks. Big and bearded, he goes in velvet hung with gold and silver chains, and eats and drinks more than his humours can bear and suffers gout; the spell he invented for it dulls the pain but sours his temper, which he blames on his wife's nagging. His huge court is the centre of the covenant, its kitchens full of cooks thanks to endless silver and its halls full of guests, Hermetic, faerie, magical and mundane. He loves stories, above all tales from beyond Ireland, and gives away his bees' honey, among the best in Hibernia, to friends and allies.

His wife Aoife, kept young by strong longevity rituals, looks far younger than he. They have lately adopted a small boy into Vigil's court, whom Éinri means for House Mercere, so he may need a sponsor at one of the Mercer Houses. His talisman is a coat of bronze mail enchanted to grow with his girth; his familiar a big, lazy wolfhound. His parens Cillíni once taught a Scottish magus, Bróccín, the courtesy owed to Ireland's otherworld, a tale Éinri likes to tell.

He has a long feud with Dalton Ballaugh of Lámbaird: many certamen and clashes of their grogs, not yet Wizard War, but real loathing, odd to onlookers given how alike the two men and their covenants are, and perhaps that is the trouble.

gr_inne_inghean_uait_ar.name: Gráinne inghean Uaitéar

description.biography:
Feud: Cú Chonnacht Cluasach Mac Tire of Bjornaer. Their Wizard War has never ended, though they have met face to face many times; the Hibernian Code presumes a war goes on until death, surrender or treaty.

Feud: Guillaume Flambeau of Praesis, an old rival who longs to see her humbled.

gr_inne_inghean_uait_ar.summary:
A maga of Merinita, as boisterous as anyone at Vigil, who looks thirty-eight. She married the handsome Pádraig when both were young. Her familiar is a red kite named Úna, whose senses she shares, and her talisman a bow of many materials attuned to several effects, her second: tired of her first, a sword, she broke it in a rite and threw the pieces off the cliffs of Cionn Mhálanna. The same excess runs through her magic, for she is a Waster of Vis without much knowing it.

As quartermaster, a mostly ceremonial post, she must approve any large spending of vis, and she has charge of the vaults and their uncatalogued treasures, though like those before her she has never grown into it and has little notion what they are worth. She knows of the Verditius right to work at Vigil, which may give her the leverage to win one of the Gifted children from Connacht when the Tribunal next meets. The Two Dozen Men of Mhálanna are devoted to her. Guillaume of Praesis, whom she has slighted many times, longs to see her humbled.

m_el_ruanaid_an_doire.name: Máel-ruanaid an Doire
m_el_ruanaid_an_doire.summary:
Vigil's loremaster, of Merinita, who looks fifty: keeper of the covenant's magical traditions, a trust he takes more seriously than those before him, who let many books rot in the vaults, and the mystagogue of Merinita's Folk Mysteries for his sodales. His master taught him divination, the secret of Banbha's Crown, and spells to command the covenant's bees, guide their flight and use their senses; when he seems to know the unknowable, that is likely how.

A master of Merinita Story Magic, he understands the power of symbols and believes Qui Sonant's magic rests not on the songs but on the symbolic act of singing; if he could learn it, the symbols of the Folk Mysteries might be freed from needing a physical form. His fellows find him a little dull, without their sense of fun. His familiar is an owl of like temper; his talisman a skull he found in the vaults and plated in silver.

maoilfhinn_in_mac_lir.name: Maoilfhinnéin mac Lir
maoilfhinn_in_mac_lir.summary: The Ambassador to the Sea, a magus of Merinita who looks fifty and spends much of his time at faerie and magical courts. His talisman is a staff of sea-unicorn horn, his familiar a porpoise, and his wife a faerie princess of Inishtrahull. With his long white hair and beard and his sturdy frame he looks like some old sea god, a likeness he plays up to keep eyes off what he is really doing.
maoilfhinn_in_mac_lir.secrets: He believes the old stories must repeat, that the Ordo Hiberniae will be driven back as the native wizards were, and sees the first signs already. Should Vigil come under threat, all is ready for the cathach to go to Inishtrahull and the covenant to be rebuilt on the island. Meanwhile he backs Lámbaird's views at Tribunal to mend the harm Éinri has done; he feeds Gráinne's overconfidence, knowing a sacrifice may soon be needed; and his allies in the sea have brought him the shards of her first talisman, which he has fixed as an Arcane Connection and is steering into the hands of Guillaume of Praesis.

peter.name: Peter

description.biography: Feud: Lewis of Verditius, the master stonemason of Qui Sonant, who drove him out over Ingasia's claim to be the House's domus magna.

peter.summary: A Verditius stonemason who once worked at Qui Sonant beside Lewis. They fell out over Ingasia's claim to be Verditius's domus magna; when Finn took Lewis's side, Peter left, and he now wanders, nursing a vendetta he is about to escalate. He may exploit Lewis's warnings to rivals over one of the Coill Trí's Gifted children. Without a covenant he is a vagrant in Hibernian law. The book gives no age.

bressal_ua_bonis_geas.name: Bressal Ua Boniségeas
bressal_ua_bonis_geas.summary: Bressal of Bonisagus, who has studied the peat moor of Beaghmore at length and holds that its warring auras are a shattered regio, broken by design or by accident. The book names no covenant for him and gives no age.

ballack.name: Ballack
ballack.summary:
Lord of Praesis, a Tytalus from the Rhine who looks sixty-five; Holzner was his filius. He delighted in turning Hibernia's own customs on the Irish and taking his revenge on Meadhbh, yet it says something of him that Holzner's head still hangs from the palisade exactly where she hung it. He despises the Irish magi and their old ways, and is courting the established English covenants and the newcomers alike.

He has spent the past year tightening his grip on the ruins, but the war cost him dearly. His own resources are gone, he owes vis and favours to a number of magi, and he has had to borrow more vis and casting tablets from far-off backers. For all his swagger he knows his prize is only on loan until he pays, so he is hunting for a way to make the covenant pay its way; he cannot be seen to give it up.

b_et_in_ua_traimair.name: Báetáin Ua Traimair
b_et_in_ua_traimair.summary:
The traitor of Praesis, who looks forty-seven: one of the besieged, he lost faith in Meadhbh as the siege grew hopeless and, choosing a Praesis that survived over one destroyed, handed the Gáe Bulg to Ballack. When the others found out, they knew the fight was lost and fled.

One of the few Irish-born magi of House Tremere, he has spent his whole life at Praesis; years ago his parens went into retirement at Coeris and took Báetáin's sigil with him. He seldom leaves the old tower now, for every walk takes him past the burnt homes of people he knew, and he still hears their screams as fire fell from the sky; he lives under one roof with Guillaume, who killed them. Still, Praesis stands, and can be rebuilt.

guillaume_of_normandy.name: Guillaume of Normandy

description.biography: Feud: Gráinne inghean Uaitéar of Vigil, who has slighted him many times; he wants nothing more than to see her humbled.

guillaume_of_normandy.summary:
Guillaume Flambeau of Normandy, who looks fifty-two. He could never get out from under the shadow of Montverte, where he was apprenticed, and came to Hibernia ten years ago to make his name, drawn by stories heard as an apprentice. He is frighteningly good with Ignem. He has already taken the cathach of an independent magus, and with it that magus's resources and his apprentice, whom he is shaping in his own image.

He is striking at places in Connacht through the Bréifne mercenaries he pays, who find vis sources and raid them; he has not crossed the border himself yet. Gráinne inghean Uaitéar of Vigil has long been his rival, and he would love to see the witch brought low before him.

cacht.name: Cacht
cacht.summary:
Cacht of the Cultas Críamoine, who looks forty: a Hibernian-born maga raised at Qui Sonant and chosen by the Path of Strife. Turning from her House's usual morality drew her to conflict, and the siege offered a rare test, the overthrow of the way things were. She killed for Ballack, then lost interest in his goals.

She has no cause of her own and stays at Praesis only until one finds her, but she listens closely to Guillaume's reports on Connacht, scenting a new war in the making.

meadhbh.name: Meadhbh
meadhbh.summary:
The fallen leader of Praesis, now in sanctuary at Qui Sonant Pro Quieto, whose lands the Treaty makes a haven for all. When Holzner stole the Gáe Bulg she had him caught and executed and hung his head by its hair from the palisade; she held Praesis through a year's siege until Báetáin gave the spear away for her safe passage. Her druid allies had already left her, saying her demands had grown unreasonable. At Praesis they meet weekly to guess where she and her supporters are and whether they will come back.

The book gives neither her House (Ex Miscellanea is assumed) nor her age.

faol_n.name: Faolán
faol_n.summary: A magus of the Younger House (Ex Miscellanea) who fled into Connacht before Praesis fell and has stayed far longer than three nights, a plain breach of the Treaty. His parens was one of the true Ollamhain, and he has only a weak grasp of the Hermetic Arts, so he feels nearer the Connacht druids than the Order; he may have friends among the Coill Trí. He belongs to no covenant, a vagrant at law.
faol_n.secrets: He is turning his back on the Order. The Tribunal has not yet worked out where he is; when it does, it will want him brought back, with or without the Coill Trí's help.
